SIR, IT has been determined by the President of the United States, that under present circumstances, it has become necessary to modify the instructions issued from this department on the 8th day of April 1797, in such manner as no longer to restrain vessels of the United States from sailing in an armed condition, when destined to be employed in a regular and lawful commerce'. The Treasury's own words.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1798 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The President's proclamation of 23 March 1798 for a day of solemn humiliation, fasting and prayer
new_groups.definition: Printings of the proclamation: 'BY THE President of the United States of America, A PROCLAMATION. As the safety and prosperity of nations ultimately and essentially depend on the protection and the blessing of Almighty God; and the national acknowledgment of this truth is not only an indispensable duty which the people owe to him, but a duty whose natural influence is favorable to the promotion of that Morality and Piety, without which social Happiness cannot exist'. The President's own words.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1798 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The President's message of 3 April 1798 laying the envoys' instructions and dispatches before Congress
new_groups.definition: Printings of the message: 'In compliance with the request of the House of Representatives, expressed in their resolution of the 2d of this month, I transmit to both Houses the instructions to and dispatches from the Envoys Extraordinary of the United States to the French Republic, which were mentioned in my message of the 19th of March last, omitting only some names, and a few expressions descriptive of the persons'. The President's own words.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1798 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The Senate, April 1798: a motion for a committee on removing aliens who may be dangerous, and on returns of aliens landed
new_groups.definition: Printings of a motion made in the Senate: 'Resolved, That a committee be appointed to consider whether any and what provision ought to be made by law, for removing from the territory of the United States, such aliens born, not entitled by the constitution and laws thereof, to the rights of citizenship, as may be dangerous to its peace and safety'. A motion in Congress, as the papers printed it.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1798 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Berne, 5 March 1798: General Schauenburg's letter on the French troops' entry into the city
new_groups.definition: Printings of a letter: 'Copy of a letter from General Schauenburg, commander of the French troops. Berne, March 5. We yesterday entered this city. An engagement took place, which continued for three hours, and was on both sides obstinately contested. The Swissers have lost many men. We have taken 20 cannon and 9 colours'. The French commander's own account, as the papers printed it.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1798 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Amsterdam, 20 March 1798: the American consul's letter that the ship America, brought in by a French cruiser, has been released
new_groups.definition: Printings of a letter: 'Consular Office of the United States of America, Amsterdam, March 20. Mr. Benjamin Russell, Boston, SIR, I AVAIL myself of the first opportunity to acquaint you that the ship America, Capt. Henshaw, from New-York, lately brought in here by a French cruiser, has been immediately released by the Consul of that nation'. The consul's own words, from a Boston paper.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1798 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The act of May 1798 more effectually to protect the commerce and coasts of the United States
new_groups.definition: Printings of the act: 'AN ACT More effectually to protect the Commerce and Coasts of the United States. WHEREAS armed vessels, sailing under authority, or pretence of authority, from the Republic of France, have committed depredations on the commerce of the United States, and have recently captured the vessels and property of citizens thereof, on and near the coasts'. An act of Congress, as the papers printed it; the Senate's bill, printed earlier in other words ('armed vessels belonging to the Republic of France'), is counted apart (X-1809-07).

new_groups.label: The House, 6 June 1798: Mr. Dwight Foster's resolutions that the French Republic has violated the treaties
new_groups.definition: Printings of the resolutions laid before the House of Representatives: 'WHEREAS the French Republic, regardless of those principles of good faith which ought to ensure a due observance of treaties, have, in various instances, violated the express stipulation of the treaties heretofore made or subsisting between the United States and the French nation ... Resolved, That it is expedient to make a legislative declaration'. Resolutions moved in Congress, as the papers printed them; Mr. Blount's resolutions in the same words on Great Britain are another text (C-07).
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1798 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The President's message of 21 June 1798 on General Marshall's arrival, communicating Mr. Gerry's letter
new_groups.definition: Printings of the message: 'WHILE I congratulate you on the arrival of General Marshall, one of our late Envoys Extraordinary to the French Republic, at a place of safety, where he is justly held in honor, I think it my duty to communicate to you a letter received by him from Mr. Gerry, the only one of the three who has not received a congé'. The President's own words.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1798 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Philadelphia, July 1798: reports that the Delaware sloop of war, Captain Decatur, has captured a French privateer schooner off Egg Harbour
new_groups.definition: Printings of a Philadelphia paragraph in two forms: 'We have the satisfaction to announce to our readers that the Delaware sloop of war, capt. Decatur, (who only went out to sea on Friday) on Saturday evening captured a French privateer schooner of 12 guns and 70 men, close in with Egg-Harbour', and 'Yesterday Capt. Decatur, of the United States Sloop Delaware arrived at the Navy-Office. He informs, that the Delaware sailed on Friday last, and on Saturday evening captured a French privateer schooner of 12 guns and 70 men, close in with Egg Harbour'. Reports at second hand, in the papers' words.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1798 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The President's message to the Senate of 18 July 1798 with General Washington's letter accepting the command of the army
new_groups.definition: Printings of the message: 'BELIEVING that the letter received this morning from General WASHINGTON will give high satisfaction to the Senate, I transmit them a copy of it, and congratulate them and the public on this great event, the General's acceptance of his appointment, as Lieutenant General and Commander in Chief of the army', with the General's letter from Mount-Vernon of 13 July. The President's and the General's own words.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1798 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The act of 14 July 1798 in addition to the act for the punishment of certain crimes against the United States (sedition)

BE it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America, in Congress assembled, That if any persons shall unlawfully combine or conspire together, with intent to oppose any measure or measures of the government of the United States, which are or shall be directed by proper authority'. A report from French papers, at second hand.

new_groups.label: Paris, 12 July 1798: the French minister of foreign relations' letter to Mr. Gerry, enclosing his passport

We are taught to expect the arrival of 40,000 men; they now speak but of 20,000. The other 20,000 are to go by the Isle of Cyprus to Aleppo, and from thence to pass by the Euphrates to the Persian Gulf'. A letter of an unnamed writer, at second hand, as the papers printed it.

dispositions_summary.method: The automatic families first printed in 1798 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 387 items, 83 in 4 or more papers by the finder's count), and the families of 1797 were looked for on the 1798 pages (items_from_1797.json). Every item in 3 or more papers was counted by machine by about 100 words of its text from the finder's position, over all 1,656 pages in both transcriptions (a dense run of its word 5-grams, at least a quarter of them); the counts were joined into documents where two items stand at the same place on the same pages, or where two documents titled by the same opening stand on mostly the same pages. Every item the machine put in every surviving paper, and the news considered for choosing, was counted again by about 70 words from its own opening, the acts of Congress by their first section's own words (counts_1798.json), and every page found was read; the bills printed before the acts they became, in other words, are counted apart. Each admitted printing was checked against its page scan.

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: Counted by their own words, 43 items of 1798 are eligible: 29 in 4 papers, 12 in 5, 2 in 6, 0 in 7. 4 items are printed by every paper that survives for their weeks and are admitted; 21 more are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news (one affair's items under a parent story, X-1800-01). 11 more eligible items counted by their opening are not chosen, and 6 documents of the item finder are eligible by their own words and not chosen; all are listed with their counts. 5 candidates counted by their opening are below the bar and listed. 172 more documents of the item finder are below the bar by their own words (docs_1798.json); they are not listed one by one. The bills counted apart from their acts, the act printed in full by one paper and the documents of the item finder that stand at the enacting formula are listed as read.
counted_item_by_item.Titles of the items not chosen: Each eligible document of the item finder not chosen is listed by its own words: the dateline or heading before the finder's position and the words that follow (some begin inside the item, where the finder's position does); a notice or advertisement that names a private person is described instead (R-04). Each candidate counted by its opening is listed by a title of the review's.
